issues.finding: The second public reference labels its source sections Language obstacles; Pacifier-free care; SIDS guidelines for sleep. The first two are editorial descriptions, whereas the original subsection headings are Remove obstacles (PDF 131, continuing through the cited pacifier text on PDF 132) and Consider going pacifier-free (PDF 199). The foundation source-reference contract requires the source subsection heading as printed, allowing normalized whitespace. The cited physical pages and underlying claims are correct; this is a narrow source-location label defect.
issues.requiredCorrection: Change this reference's section string to the original headings, for example Remove obstacles; Consider going pacifier-free; SIDS guidelines for sleep. Keep the current valid claim page spans and locator; no care-prose change is required by this finding. Freeze and review the changed reference projection before treating this issue as resolved.

textPlacement.assessment: The care prose is source-faithful. Both topic rows independently state the authors' discouragement of constant use alongside possible SIDS reduction and limited use for settling/sleep; neither row implies an absolute ban. Detail preserves the communication rationale, acknowledges an unsettled or sleep-bound baby, and explicitly dates the sleep-safety box to the 2021 book instead of presenting its list as independently current guidance. Attribution remains visible, there are no steps or added soothing/sleep instructions, and the 6–9-month placement is a browsing context rather than an age deadline. The complete source cessation discussion, preferred first-year timing, alternative-soothing list and thumb/finger comparison were read; this bounded entry offers no cessation plan and does not convert those suggestions into a new protocol. The only required correction is the second reference's subsection labels.

textPlacement.assessment: The exact 6–9-month placement faithfully presents the adult's role in the complete Sharing unit. In both topic summaries the adult notices whether the baby seems ready to move on or seems to want to keep playing and explains that apparent wish; it does not instruct the adult to retrieve an object, force relinquishment, or announce an inferred feeling as fact. Detail keeps both first-year possibilities and the reciprocal case in which the baby reaches for another child's object. Asking if that child is finished and waiting/watching/finding another object preserve the PDF 215 continuation as possibilities, without promising immediate learning or cooperation. Public age context distinguishes first-year exploration from the source's discussion around 12–16 months, and its separate browsing note prevents the 6–9 label from becoming a sharing or ownership milestone. The Sharing heading and PDF 214–215 reference correctly identify the complete unit. No additional qualification is necessary to make these specific short and detail surfaces faithful.
